DVMP_xsec module

Deeply Virtual Meson Production (DVMP) cross-section calculations.

This module implements the differential cross-sections and the \(R = \sigma_L / \sigma_T\) ratio for exclusive meson production (\(\rho^0\), \(\phi\), \(J/\psi\)) off the proton. The cross-sections are expressed in terms of helicity Transition Form Factors (TFFs) \(\mathcal{H}\) and \(\mathcal{E}\) computed from GPDs.

Key components:

  • R() — L/T ratio parametrization (Eq. (32) of

    arXiv:1112.2597).

  • R_rho_fit() — iMinuit fit of R parameters to combined H1+ZEUS data.

  • R_fitted() — best-fit \(R\) with propagated uncertainty.

  • dsigmaL_DVMP_dt() — longitudinal differential cross-section \(d\sigma_L/dt\).

  • dsigma_DVMP_dt() — total \(d\sigma/dt\) after L/T unseparation.

gumpgpd.DVMP_xsec.MassCorr(meson: int) → float[source]

Meson mass correction entering the propagator denominator.

Returns \(M_{J/\psi}\) for \(J/\psi\) production and 0 for lighter mesons, where the mass correction to \(Q^2\) is negligible.

Parameters:

meson (int) – meson code — 1 for \(\rho^0\), 2 for \(\phi\), 3 for \(J/\psi\).

Returns:

mass correction in GeV (\(M_{J/\psi}\) for meson=3, 0 otherwise).

Return type:

float

gumpgpd.DVMP_xsec.R(Q: float, a: float, p: float, meson: int) → float[source]

L/T cross-section ratio \(R = \sigma_L / \sigma_T\) parametrization.

For \(\rho^0\) (meson=1) the parametrization follows Eq. (32) of arXiv:1112.2597:

\[R(Q) = \frac{Q^2}{M_{\rho}^2}\left(1 + e^a \frac{Q^2}{M_{\rho}^2}\right)^{-p}\]

For \(J/\psi\) (meson=3) the simple ratio \(Q^2 / M_{J/\psi}^2\) is used.

Parameters:

  • Q (float) – photon virtuality \(Q\) in GeV.

  • a (float) – fit parameter controlling the transition scale.

  • p (float) – fit parameter controlling the power-law fall-off.

  • meson (int) – meson code — 1 for \(\rho^0\), 3 for \(J/\psi\); 2 is reserved for \(\phi\).

Returns:

\(R = \sigma_L / \sigma_T\).

Return type:

float

gumpgpd.DVMP_xsec.R_fitted(Q: float, meson: int = 1) → tuple[source]

Evaluate the fitted R() ratio with propagated \(1\sigma\) uncertainty.

Calls R_rho_fit() to obtain best-fit parameters, then propagates their uncertainties analytically via first-order error propagation:

\[\sigma_R^2 = \left(\frac{\partial R}{\partial a}\right)^2 \sigma_a^2 + \left(\frac{\partial R}{\partial p}\right)^2 \sigma_p^2 + 2\,\frac{\partial R}{\partial a}\frac{\partial R}{\partial p}\, \mathrm{cov}(a,\,p)\]
Parameters:

  • Q (float) – photon virtuality in GeV (scalar or array).

  • meson (int) – meson code; currently only 1 (\(\rho^0\)) is implemented.

Returns:

(R_mean, R_std) — central value and \(1\sigma\) uncertainty of \(R(Q)\).

Return type:

tuple

gumpgpd.DVMP_xsec.R_rho_cost(a: float, p: float) → float[source]

Reduced \(\chi^2\) cost function for fitting R() to combined H1+ZEUS \(\rho\) data.

Parameters:

  • a (float) – fit parameter \(a\) of R().

  • p (float) – fit parameter \(p\) of R().

Returns:

\(\chi^2_{\rm red} = \sum_i [(R_i^{\rm exp} - R_i^{\rm pred}) / \sigma_i]^2 \,/\, N_{\rm dof}\).

Return type:

float

gumpgpd.DVMP_xsec.R_rho_fit() → tuple[source]

Fit R() parameters (a, p) to the combined H1+ZEUS \(\rho\) data.

Uses iMinuit migrad for minimization and hesse for uncertainty estimation. The result is cached so the fit runs only once per session.

Returns:

(val_a, var_a, val_p, var_p, corr_ap) where

  • val_a — best-fit value of \(a\)

  • var_a — \(1\sigma\) uncertainty on \(a\)

  • val_p — best-fit value of \(p\)

  • var_p — \(1\sigma\) uncertainty on \(p\)

  • corr_ap — covariance between \(a\) and \(p\)

Return type:

tuple

gumpgpd.DVMP_xsec.epsilon(y: float) → float[source]

Virtual photon polarization parameter \(\varepsilon\).

\[\varepsilon = \frac{1 - y}{1 - y + y^2/2}\]

See Eq. (31) of arXiv:1112.2597.

Parameters:

y (float) – inelasticity (beam energy loss fraction).

Returns:

\(\varepsilon \in (0, 1)\).

Return type:

float
